```{r}
#| echo: false

library(dplyr)

df_encoded <- df %>%
  mutate(
    # Binary: Male = 0, Female = 1
    part_time_job = ifelse(part_time_job== "No",1,0),
    extracurricular_participation = ifelse(extracurricular_participation== "Yes",1,0),

    gender = ifelse(gender == "Male", 0, 1),
    
    # Ordinal: poor = 0, average = 1, good = 2
    internet_quality = case_when(
      internet_quality == "Poor" ~ 0,
      internet_quality == "Average" ~ 1,
      internet_quality == "Good" ~ 2
    ),
    
    # Same ordinal encoding
    diet_quality = case_when(
      diet_quality == "Poor" ~ 0,
      diet_quality == "Fair" ~ 1,
      diet_quality == "Good" ~ 2
    ),
    
    # Ordinal: None = 0, High School = 1, Bachelor = 2, Master = 3
    parental_education_level = case_when(
      parental_education_level == "None" ~ 0,
      parental_education_level == "High School" ~ 1,
      parental_education_level == "Bachelor" ~ 2,
      parental_education_level == "Master" ~ 3
    )
  )
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-align: center
#| results: hide
rec_df <- recipe(~.,data = df_encoded) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) 

rec_df

kmeans_spec <- k_means(num_clusters = tune())

kmeans_wf <- workflow(rec_df, kmeans_spec)

kmeans_wf <- kmeans_wf %>% 
  update_model(kmeans_spec)

grid <- tibble(num_clusters = 1:10)

set.seed(123)
boots <- bootstraps(df_encoded, times = 10)

res <- tune_cluster(
  kmeans_wf,
  resamples = boots,
  grid = grid,
  metrics = cluster_metric_set(sse_within_total, sse_total, sse_ratio)
)

res_metrics <- collect_metrics(res)%>% print(n=Inf)

best <- res %>%
  select_best(metric="sse_ratio")  ###Observese que este criterio es un poco "chafa", ya que esta medida
best                               ### en general va decreciendo con el aumento en el valor de K

```
Para k-means vamos a determinar por medio del método del codo y de la silueta el número adecuado de clusters que necesitamos:

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| fig-align: center
#| results: hide
#| fig-width: 18
#| fig-height: 6

library(gridExtra)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidymodels)
library(tidyclust)

# Define school colors
green <- "#2E8B57"
red <- "#DC143C"
gold <- "#FFD700"

# Plot 1: SSE Ratio without CV
p1 <- res_metrics %>%
  filter(.metric == "sse_ratio") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = num_clusters, y = mean)) +
  geom_point(color = green, size = 3) +
  geom_line(color = red, size = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  ylab("mean WSS/TSS ratio") +
  xlab("Número de clusters") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  ggtitle("A) Gráfica de codo K-MEANS") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = green, face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(color = green, size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(color = red, size = 8),
    panel.grid = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3)
  )

# Plot 2: SSE Ratio with CV
p2 <- res1_metrics %>%
  filter(.metric == "sse_ratio") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = num_clusters, y = mean)) +
  geom_point(color = green, size = 3) +
  geom_line(color = red, size = 1) +
  theme_minimal() +
  ylab("mean WSS/TSS ratio cv") +
  xlab("Number of clusters") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  ggtitle("B) Gráfica de codo K-MEANS con CV") +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = green, face = "bold", size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(color = green, size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(color = red, size = 8),
    panel.grid = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3)
  )

# Plot 3: Silhouette Method
p3 <- ggplot(metrics_df, aes(x = num_clusters, y = mean)) +
  geom_line(color = green, size = 1) +
  geom_point(color = red, size = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "C) Silhouette Method",
    subtitle = "k = 2 to 10, 10 folds",
    x = "Número de Clusters (k)",
    y = "Promedio Silhouette Score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = green, face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = gold, size = 9),
    axis.title = element_text(color = green, size = 10),
    axis.text = element_text(color = red, size = 8),
    panel.grid = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3)
  )

# Arrange in 1x3 grid (side by side)
grid.arrange(p1, p2, p3, ncol = 3,
             top = textGrob("Métodos para Determinar el Número Óptimo de Clusters", 
                            gp = gpar(col = green, fontface = "bold", fontsize = 14)))

```
Podemos apreciar entonces:

- Para la primera gráfica, el número adecuado es 4
- Para la segunda parece ser 5
- Para la tercera es 3

No es consistente. Veamos más pruebas.


```{r}

#| echo: false
#| message: false
#| warning: false
#| results: hide
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-width: 18
#| fig-height: 10

library(tidymodels)
library(dplyr)

# Define school colors
green <- "#2E8B57"
red <- "#DC143C"
gold <- "#FFD700"

recipe_df <- recipe(~., data = df_encoded) %>%
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors()) %>%
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) 

kmeans_df <- k_means(num_clusters = 3)

kmeans_df_wf <- workflow(recipe_df, kmeans_df)

kmeans_df_fit <- fit(kmeans_df_wf, data = df_encoded)

# Get clustered data
clustered_data <- augment(kmeans_df_fit, new_data = df_encoded)

# Add exam_score from original df
clustered_data <- clustered_data %>%
  bind_cols(df %>% select(exam_score))

# Get centroids (these don't have exam_score)
centroids <- tidy(kmeans_df_fit)

# Plot using only the variables available in centroids
# The centroids won't have exam_score, so we need to plot something else
ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = clustered_data, 
             aes(x = scale(study_hours_per_day), y = scale(exam_score), color = .pred_cluster), 
             alpha = 0.6, size = 2.5) +
  # Remove the centroids from the plot since they don't have exam_score
  scale_color_manual(values = c(green, red, gold)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "K-Means Clustering",
    subtitle = "Número de grupos: k = 3",
    x = "Horas de Estudio (escalado)",
    y = "Resultado Examen (escalado)",
    color = "Cluster"
  ) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(color = green, face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(color = gold, size = 11),
    axis.title = element_text(color = green, size = 11),
    axis.text = element_text(color = red, size = 9),
    legend.title = element_text(color = gold, face = "bold"),
    legend.text = element_text(color = green),
    panel.grid = element_line(color = "gray90", size = 0.3),
    panel.border = element_rect(color = green, fill = NA, size = 0.5)
  )
```

  summarise(num_users = n()) %>%
